# Persistent Memory MCP

Persistent Memory MCP is an open-source Python Model Context Protocol server for durable software-project memory and measurable context compilation across AI coding tools.

Documentation: https://dannymaaz.github.io/memory-mcp/
Repository: https://github.com/dannymaaz/memory-mcp
Package: persistent-memory-mcp
Command: memory-mcp
License: MIT
Author: Danny Maaz

## Purpose
It stores project architecture, technical decisions, tasks, warnings, checkpoints, file relationships, timeline events and session state. Compatible MCP clients can retrieve the same project context in later sessions.

The post-v0.3 Context Compiler filters, ranks, verifies and packs memory/repository evidence under a hard token budget instead of returning unbounded project history.

## Clients
Codex, Claude Code, Claude Desktop, OpenCode, Qwen Code and other clients with standard MCP server configuration.

## Storage and search
SQLite is the default local-first backend. Supabase/PostgreSQL remain optional self-managed extras. Search supports semantic retrieval with deterministic lexical/local fallback.

## Context Compiler
Context Packet v1 records provenance, verification state, final serialized token count, tokenizer/model identity and per-block selection metrics.

Progressive repository retrieval expands map -> files -> symbols -> exact line fragments with Git/file SHA-256 provenance and explicit byte/token limits.

Persistent symbol evolution stores commit-scoped symbol snapshots and classified added/modified/moved/renamed/deleted changes without storing unbounded source bodies. Evidence can be verified, stale, contradicted, missing_source or unverified.

## Quality regression gates
MEM-39 / PR #66 introduced deterministic local quality gates over a versioned non-sensitive coding-task corpus. Quality #262 completed this milestone.

Measured metrics include file recall@5, symbol recall@8, precision, hard token fit, token savings, provenance coverage, latency and safety pass rate. Initial v1 baseline has full recall, token-fit and provenance coverage with 77.22% average token savings against the supported-repository baseline.

Hard adversarial gates cover expired/untrusted memory, prompt injection, dirty repository cursor invalidation, rename identity continuity, contradicted evidence retention and stale evidence after dirty Git changes.

Public evaluation contract: https://github.com/dannymaaz/memory-mcp/blob/main/docs/CONTEXT_QUALITY.md

## Operational project map and Galaxy
MEM-40 / PR #68 adds a bounded owner-scoped operational projection over the existing SQLite project state and persistent code-symbol evidence.

The read model provides a global project overview plus project impact graphs using project -> repository -> file -> symbol -> task/decision/evidence relationships when persisted links exist. Nodes expose compact risk and verification metadata rather than full source or memory bodies.

Verification states: verified, stale, contradicted, missing_source, unverified.
Risk projection: critical, high, medium, low, none.

Current-change filtering uses only the latest persisted snapshot run for each repository and keeps the affected code/evidence area without project-wide fan-out.

Local operational endpoints:
- /api/operational/projects
- /api/operational/graph?project_id=<id>
- /api/operational/export.json?project_id=<id>
- /galaxy/operational?project_id=<id>

Owner resolution fails closed: configured OWNER_ID wins; otherwise an owner is inferred only when exactly one project owner exists. Multiple owners without explicit configuration are rejected instead of mixed.

The operational surface is localhost-only and read-only. It does not execute repository code, mutate project state or expose full content bodies/absolute repository roots. Short labels use existing secret redaction.

The cross-platform bounds fixture contains 20 projects, 120 symbols across 12 files and 20 tasks. The full graph remains 154 nodes / 173 edges, while changed-only reduces it to 55 / 74. Observed reference full-graph time was 6.26 ms Ubuntu, 8.08 ms Windows and 8.56 ms macOS, with a deliberately non-flaky 5,000 ms CI ceiling.

Public operational-map contract: https://github.com/dannymaaz/memory-mcp/blob/main/docs/OPERATIONAL_MAP.md

## Installation
pipx install persistent-memory-mcp
memory-mcp init
memory-mcp doctor
memory-mcp health

Default local database: ~/.memory-mcp/memory.db

## Relationship to Git
Git stores code history. Persistent Memory MCP stores project reasoning and working state while persisting bounded Git-grounded provenance so later agents can distinguish current verified source evidence from stale or contradicted historical context. The operational map projects that persisted evidence state; it does not independently run live Git verification on every dashboard request.
